The caterpillar eats the fruits in the order $1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3, \dots$, so after eating $w$ fruits the eaten interval is $[-\lfloor w/2\rfloor, \lceil w/2\rceil]$. Its length is $w$, so each trip from one end of the eaten interval to the new fruit on the far side covers $w+1$ units. For example, at $w=1$ he goes from $1$ to $-1$, a distance of $2$.

While his weight is $w$, he moves at $2^{-w}$ units per day, so the trip that raises his weight from $w$ to $w+1$ takes $(w+1)\,2^{-w}$ days. The total time to reach 10 pounds is

$$
T=\sum_{w=0}^{9}\frac{w+1}{2^{w}}=\sum_{n=1}^{10}\frac{n}{2^{n-1}}.
$$

Using the partial-sum formula $\sum_{n=1}^{N} n x^{n-1}=\dfrac{1-(N+1)x^N+Nx^{N+1}}{(1-x)^2}$ with $x=\tfrac12$ and $N=10$:

$$
T=4\left(1-\frac{11}{1024}+\frac{5}{1024}\right)=4\cdot\frac{1018}{1024}=\frac{509}{128}.
$$

Check: the decimal terms sum to $3.9765625$, and $509/128=3.9765625$.

So he weighs 10 pounds after $\dfrac{509}{128}$ days.

ANSWER: 509/128
